use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::protocol::{FiltersState, Track, VoiceState};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Session {
    pub session_id: String,
    pub bot_user_id: String,
    pub client_name: String,
    pub resumed: bool,
    pub created_at_ms: i64,
    pub last_seen_at_ms: i64,
    pub resume_enabled: bool,
    pub timeout_secs: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct PlayerKey {
    pub session_id: String,
    pub guild_id: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PlayerState {
    pub key: PlayerKey,
    pub bot_user_id: String,
    pub voice: Option<VoiceState>,
    pub track: Option<Track>,
    pub paused: bool,
    pub volume: u16,
    pub position_ms: i64,
    pub connected: bool,
    pub filters: FiltersState,
    pub queue: Option<PlayerQueue>,
    pub end_time_ms: Option<i64>,
    pub created_at_ms: i64,
    pub updated_at_ms: i64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct PlayerQueue {
    pub enabled: bool,
    pub tracks: std::collections::VecDeque<Track>,
    pub repeat_mode: RepeatMode,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub enum RepeatMode {
    #[default]
    Off,
    Track,
    Queue,
}

    pub fn new(key: PlayerKey, bot_user_id: String, now_ms: i64) -> Self {

Done. Since `build_stats` is the single constructor for `StatsPayload`, both the WebSocket `STATS` message and `GET /v4/stats` now emit `pausedPlayers` and `disconnectedPlayers`.

Changes made in `services/kenalink-rs`:
- `src/protocol.rs`: added `paused_players`/`disconnected_players` fields to `StatsPayload` (camelCase-serialized automatically).
- `src/state/mod.rs`: added `paused_players`/`disconnected_players` to the `StateStore` trait.
- `src/state/memory.rs`: implemented both — paused counts players with a loaded track that are paused; disconnected counts players with `connected == false`.
- `src/api_ws/mod.rs`: `build_stats` now populates the two new counters.

No existing tests covered `total_players`/`playing_players`, so I didn't add new test scaffolding to stay consistent with the current repo conventions.
